chunks.title: Writing a tscircuit board — The shape of a board module
chunks.text:
A board file exports a single default React component. The root element is `<board>`; every
other element must be inside it.

```tsx
export default () => (
  <board width="40mm" height="25mm">
    <pinheader name="J1" pinCount={2} pcbX={-15} pcbY={0} schX={-8} schY={0} />
    <resistor name="R1" resistance="330" footprint="0603" pcbX={0} pcbY={0} schX={0} schY={0} />
    <trace from=".J1 > .pin1" to=".R1 > .pin1" />
  </board>
)
```

There must be no imports, no `require`, no top-level side effects and no network access: the
compile sandbox rejects source that reaches for anything outside tscircuit.

chunks.title: Writing a tscircuit board — Every component needs a name and both coordinate systems
chunks.text:
`name` is the reference designator and is required — the checks and the BOM are keyed on it.
`pcbX`/`pcbY` place the part on the board in millimetres; `schX`/`schY` place it on the
schematic. A component with only `pcbX`/`pcbY` will not appear in the schematic, and one
with only `schX`/`schY` will not appear in the PCB.

chunks.title: Writing a tscircuit board — Values are strings, geometry is numbers
chunks.text:
`resistance="330"`, `capacitance="100nF"`, `voltage="5V"` are parsed strings and accept
engineering suffixes: `1k`, `4k7`, `100nF`, `10uF`, `1meg`. Use a plain number for
`resistance="330"`; do not write `resistance={330}` with a unit in a string prop.

chunks.title: Writing a tscircuit board — A part that is not routed is a blocking error
chunks.text:
`source_traces_have_pcb_traces` fails the export gate for any `<trace>` that has no matching
`pcb_trace`. Either give the trace a `pcbRoute`, or place the connected parts close enough
for the autorouter to connect them. An explicitly unrouted trace is reported as
`pcb_trace_missing_error`, which blocks fabrication.

chunks.title: Writing a tscircuit board — Pin selectors
chunks.text:
`from` and `to` take a selector: `".J1 > .pin1"` means pin 1 of J1. Selector syntax is
documented under the `port-and-net-selectors` topic. A `pinheader` exposes `.pin1`,
`.pin2`, … and also named pins from `pinLabels`.

chunks.title: Checks and fabrication rules — What blocks an export
chunks.text:
The fabrication gate is closed while any finding has severity `error`. Two families produce
them: tscircuit's own design-rule checks, and the fab-capability rules this app adds.

chunks.title: Checks and fabrication rules — Fab capability rules
chunks.text:
For the preset the design is checked against:

- `board.size` — a `<board>` with no fixed `width`/`height` cannot be fabricated
- `board.min_side` / `board.max_side` — the envelope must be inside the fab's range
- `board.layers` — more copper layers than the fab builds
- `board.outline_mismatch` — a hand-authored `outline` that disagrees with `width`/`height`
- `fab_trace_width` — a `pcb_trace` narrower than the fab's minimum
- `fab_via_pad` / `fab_annular_ring` — a via with too little copper around the hole
- `fab_hole_min` / `fab_hole_max` — a drill outside the fab's range

The default preset is the conservative intersection of two low-cost 2-layer fabs: 0.2 mm
trace and space, 0.4 mm minimum drill, 2 layers, 10–150 mm per side. A design that passes
the default passes the cheaper named presets too.

chunks.title: Checks and fabrication rules — Rules that warn rather than block
chunks.text:
- `pcb_trace_too_long_warning` — a long trace is a signal-integrity smell, not a fab error
- `pcb_component_missing_courtyard_warning` — no courtyard, so overlap cannot be checked
- `source_no_power_pin_defined_warning` / `source_no_ground_pin_defined_warning`
- `schematic_component_styling_warning`

chunks.title: Checks and fabrication rules — Decoupling
chunks.text:
Every IC that declares a supply pin should have a capacitor within about 3 mm of that pin.
`evaluateDesign` flags a supply pin with no capacitor in range. Put the capacitor's `pcbX`
and `pcbY` within a few millimetres of the IC's matching pin, not merely on the same board.

chunks.title: Checks and fabrication rules — Placement that avoids blocking errors
chunks.text:
- Keep every part inside the board outline; a part outside it is `pcb_component_outside_board_error`
- Leave at least the fab's edge clearance (`0.5 mm` on the default preset) between a pad and the outline
- Space parts so their courtyards do not overlap
- Put a decoupling capacitor adjacent to each IC supply pin
- Give connectors an accessible orientation so they are not blocked by the board edge

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — What a footprinter string is
chunks.text:
A `footprint` prop is a compact string that footprinter (`@tscircuit/footprinter`) expands
into a pad layout. Pass the string, not a footprint object:

```tsx
<resistor name="R1" resistance="330" footprint="0603" />
<chip name="U1" footprint="soic8" />
<pinheader name="J2" pinCount={6} footprint="pinrow2_p2.54mm" />
```

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — Passives
chunks.text:
`0402`, `0603`, `0805`, `1206`, `1210` for chip resistors and capacitors. `0603` is the
safe default for hand-solderable hobby work: large enough to probe, small enough to fit.

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — Packages
chunks.text:
`soic8`, `soic14`, `soic16`, `sot23`, `sot223`, `to220`, `qfp32`, `qfn32`, `dip8`. ICs are
`<chip>`; pass the footprint as a string and set `pinLabels` so the pins can be named.

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — Connectors and headers
chunks.text:
`pinrow2_p2.54mm` is a two-row 2.54 mm header — the value is the number of pins. A 6-pin
2.54 mm header is `pinrow6_p2.54mm`. A 2.54 mm screw terminal is `screw_terminal_01x02`.

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — A string that does not exist fails the compile
chunks.text:
There is no validation step: an unrecognised footprinter string is a compile error, not a
warning. Use one of the forms above rather than inventing a package name.

chunks.title: Footprinter strings — Where footprints come from at run time
chunks.text:
Footprint strings that are not built into footprinter are fetched from the tscircuit CDN. The
compile sandbox disables that (`disableCdnLoading`) and stubs `fetch`, so **only the
built-in strings work here**. A design that needs a vendor-specific footprint cannot be
generated by this app; it is listed in docs/DECISIONS.md as a known limitation.
